projectDescription: A CLI-first, low-fi storyboarding tool: designers describe an end-to-end customer journey in prose to their coding agent, which generates an editable sketch-style storyboard website they can tweak and export to image.

roadmap.title: How Characters, Scenes & Devices Get Made
How It Plugs Into Coding Agents

decisions.title: The Storyboard File Format
decisions.caseAgainst: The story is what builds service-design empathy, and a Markdown screenplay is readable by PMs in a PR or crit; JSON is the least readable if humans ever open the file. Mitigation: JSON source of truth plus a read-only `storyboard script` Markdown view.
assumptions: The coding agent authors almost all of the file; designers tweak visually
Editor edits must write back to the file
Scene/shot/pose/mood/device vocabulary is finite and schema-able
tripwires: Designers report opening and hand-editing the file regularly -> revisit C or add a Markdown authoring layer
Validation error rate from agents stays high despite fix-it messages
decisions.summary: What file the coding agent writes, the editor edits, and the exporter reads.

decisions.title: Storyboard Art Style
decisions.caseAgainst: User stressed low fidelity; Graphite (A) reads as a rougher draft and invites critique more than Marker, which can drift toward polish and deliverable-ism. Hybrid: A's pencil + B's product-only-color rule.
assumptions: Boards travel into decks/Slack where small-size contrast matters
Core insight = where the software shows up in the day; single product color makes it visible
Characters built from modular parts favor flat fills
tripwires: Users polish boards instead of debating the journey -> roughen line weight / move toward A
decisions.summary: The drawing style every board uses, and the design tokens for the editor around it.

decisions.title: How Characters, Scenes & Devices Get Made
options: D: Modular Parts on a Rig
decisions.caseAgainst: Most expensive; 2D rigs look broken (elbows, floaty hands) before they look good and no mature open-source storyboard rig exists. A curated library ships beautiful v1 in weeks; hybrid path: draw A-style art cut into D parts from day one.
assumptions: Diverse cast AND full pose/angle range are both must-haves
Must work offline and free after install
~160 Marker Comp parts can be drawn by someone
tripwires: Rigged poses look stiff/broken in user tests -> hand-tuned pose presets only, no free joint dragging
Art production stalls -> ship front+3/4 only, add side/back later
decisions.summary: Where the cast, poses, angles, scenes and devices come from.

decisions.title: Editor Rendering Engine
decisions.caseAgainst: Building your own editor (selection, undo, snapping, zoom, touch) is a tar pit of non-differentiating work; tldraw exists to prevent that. If the tool is internal to one company, the license is cheap vs engineering time and C wins.
assumptions: Distributed free/open-source via npx with no license key
Boards stay ~a dozen panels / few hundred parts
2-4 weeks acceptable for editor basics (react-moveable for handles)
tripwires: Drag perf drops below 60fps on typical boards -> canvas art layer, keep SVG export path
decisions.summary: What draws and moves things in the browser editor.

decisions.title: How It Plugs Into Coding Agents
decisions.caseAgainst: Three surfaces can drift; C alone scored highest in the only published eval and is half the work. Start with C, add the skill when boards are valid-but-boring. Mitigation: generate AGENTS.md block + skill vocab from the CLI schema.
assumptions: Designers work in a folder where init can write files
Target agents can run shell commands
Storytelling quality matters, justifying craft guidance
tripwires: Evals show agents ignore the skill even with AGENTS.md pointer -> inline key craft rules into AGENTS.md block
Live 'edit panel 3' requests become common -> add small MCP endpoint on dev server
decisions.summary: How Claude Code, Codex, Cursor etc. learn the tool, its vocabulary and workflow.

decisions.title: Editor Layout
decisions.caseAgainst: D is the only layout that actively forces service-design thinking (feeling curve, product-presence row, workaround notes); C merely permits it and could produce happy-path marketing comics. Alternative: C with D's lanes as an exportable toggle.
assumptions: Export is the page itself
Agent does heavy composition; editor is for tweaks
Designers mostly on laptops
tripwires: Boards produced skew happy-path / no workaround panels -> promote lanes to default
decisions.summary: Where designers tweak: how the editor screen is arranged.

decisions.title: Uploaded Screens: Sketchify & Auto-Fit
decisions.caseAgainst: Teal duotone makes the screen the most prominent element, possibly stealing focus from Maya's face; and it reads as a filtered screenshot, not a drawing. C is more honestly rough for early UI. Mitigation: roughness slider + optional wireframe (trace) mode.
assumptions: UI copy matters to the story
Uploads are mostly PNG/JPG Figma exports
Product-only-teal rule applies to uploaded screens
tripwires: Users complain screens overpower characters -> lower duotone saturation default
decisions.summary: How uploaded designs become sketch-like and snap onto device screens.

decisions.title: Round-Trip & Export
options: A: Live Two-Way Sync + CLI Export
B: Save Button, Reload to Sync
decisions.caseAgainst: Live sync breeds watcher races and stale writes; v1 can be A minus conflict UI (last-write-wins per field + reload on change), adding keep-mine/take-theirs only if users hit it.
assumptions: Boards are iterated many times
Files live in git; diffs matter
Agents need headless image export
tripwires: Users report lost edits -> build per-field conflict prompt
decisions.summary: What happens to editor tweaks when the agent edits again, and how images get made.

calibration.why: Marker comp is an era-stable drawing technique; no web calibration applied.

feedback: Thought/speech bubble tails must point at the speaker's head (fixed in close-up shot); editor should auto-aim tails at the character's head anchor.

research_cache.decision7: sketchify+fit research complete (canvas Sobel+posterize bake to PNG; stored device screen quads; CSS matrix3d preview; pre-warp raster for resvg export).
